clue.text: Speech marks out quest to obtain love

indicators.note: to obtain means the jumbled letters take in and hold another piece
out signals that the letters of quest are put out of order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone sets out on a quest in search of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marks' looks like a verb in the surface, but 'Speech marks' is the whole definition; 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Quotation marks around reported words are commonly called quotes, a plural noun like speech marks.

clue.text: Police officer wearing fancy clothes lacking restraint

parts.note: someone wearing a coat is in it, so wearing gives IN

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the fancy word wraps around the officer

parts.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, ornate
DI is a Detective Inspector, a British police rank

explanation.surface: A detective goes about in flamboyant, over-the-top attire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun after 'fancy' but is a verb: the fancy word wraps the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inordinate means excessive or immoderate, beyond what is reasonable, so it describes something unrestrained.

clue.text: Converts writing style with training

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language, a form of writing

indicators.note: training is shaping or reworking, so the letters of style are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer changes how they write after some training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converts' reads as a verb but is a plural noun: people won over.
explanation.definitionFit: Proselytes are people recently brought over to a new faith or cause, so they are converts as nouns.

clue.text: Damage resulting from panic before onset of epidemic

indicators.note: the wanted letters are what comes before the epidemic's first letter in the word for panic

parts.note: a scare is a sudden fright or public panic

indicators.note: onset is the beginning, so only the first letter of epidemic is used

explanation.surface: Harm done by alarm spreading ahead of an outbreak of disease.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARE is SCAR placed before E, the onset of 'epidemic', so the part before that E is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark left by an injury, and to scar is to mar or harm, so it fits damage.

clue.text: Head started to lose heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: began is the past tense of begin, meaning started

explanation.surface: Someone gets discouraged soon after beginning a task.
explanation.walkthrough: BEGAN loses its middle letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean is informal slang for a person's head, as in being hit on the bean.

clue.text: Citroen beginning to make mobile phone system

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so the letters of Citroen move about
the beginning of make is its first letter

explanation.surface: A car maker starting to produce a mobile phone network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' rearranges CITROEN into INTERCO; 'beginning to' takes M from 'make'. 'mobile phone' reads as one phrase, but 'mobile' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercom is an internal two-way communication setup linking rooms, a telephone-like system.

clue.text: Top person of superior quality recovered more fully

definitions.meaning: the comparative of good, higher in standard
said of a patient who is in improved health after illness

explanation.surface: A leading figure of fine standing has made a stronger recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a noun for a superior, the comparative of good, and the comparative of well in the health sense.

clue.text: Messenger decapitated by good shot

indicators.note: decapitated means losing the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a runner carries messages on foot

explanation.surface: A courier is beheaded by an accurate marksman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good shot' wants to be one phrase for the definition, but 'good' gives G and 'shot' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot can mean a person who shoots, as in a fine shot, and a gunner is someone who fires guns.

clue.text: Purge lists to block extremists on committee

indicators.note: to block means to sit in the way, here lodged between the outer letters
the extremists of a word are its two end letters

parts.note: a ship that lists leans to one side

explanation.surface: A political purge where hardliners are kept off a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'committee', C and E, go round LEANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge is to rid of impurities or undesirables, and cleanse means to make clean or clear out.

clue.text: Person in temporary accommodation is more obviously affected

definitions.meaning: someone staying in a tent or caravan on holiday
camp means theatrically exaggerated, so this is its comparative

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker in a tent is being rather more theatrical.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a holidaymaker living under canvas; the other is the comparative of camp, meaning showily mannered.

clue.text: Player works naked

indicators.note: naked means stripped of covering, so both outer letters are taken off

parts.note: a works is a factory, as in a steelworks

explanation.surface: A performer strips off for a role.
explanation.walkthrough: FACTORY loses its outside letters F and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is a performer on the stage, so it is an old synonym for someone who acts in plays.

clue.text: Rigorous testing starts to reveal necessary changes

indicators.note: changes means the collected letters are altered into a new order
the starts of the two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Thorough testing begins to show where alterations are needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' gives R and N from 'reveal' and 'necessary'; 'changes' rearranges those with TESTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent describes rules or standards that are strict and exacting, which is what rigorous means.

clue.text: Potential candidates aggravated boss with spiel

indicators.note: aggravated means stirred up or worsened, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Job applicants annoyed their prospective employer with a sales pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aggravated' rearranges BOSS and SPIEL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Possibles are people who might be chosen, for example for a team, a noun use of the adjective.

clue.text: Charged items under "something for local operations providing additional services"?

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece placed under another comes after it

parts.note: summat is how a northern English local says something, a dialect form
ions are electrically charged atoms or molecules

explanation.surface: A bill listing charges under the heading of local extras.
explanation.walkthrough: SUMMAT is dialect, chiefly northern English, for something. The definition plays on 'additional': these operations add things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Summations are acts of adding numbers together, arithmetic operations whose service is addition.

clue.text: Suffer at home with effective treatment in short supply

parts.note: someone at home is said to be in

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a cure is a treatment that works

explanation.surface: A patient laid up at home when good medicine is scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short supply' cuts the last letter E from CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to bring it on oneself and undergo it, so it is close to suffer.

clue.text: Continental football players abandon position regularly

parts.note: Inter is Internazionale, the Milan football club
to leave someone is to abandon them

explanation.surface: Players from a European club walk out on their positions on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'position' reads as a footballer's role, but it is a verb in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To interleave is to insert sheets or layers at intervals between others, placing things in a regular alternation.

clue.text: Rent nondescript houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the letters are held within the word

explanation.surface: Plain, characterless homes are let out for rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent as a noun is a tear in cloth, and a rip is exactly that kind of tear.

clue.text: Is proton decaying into antimatter?

indicators.note: decaying particles break down and change, so the letters re-form

explanation.surface: A physicist wonders whether a proton breaks down into antimatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decaying' rearranges IS PROTON.
explanation.definitionFit: The particle meant is the antiparticle of the electron, a piece of antimatter, so the definition names its category.

clue.text: Crack addict's case time after time yielding nothing

indicators.note: after places the first piece behind the second
the case of a word is its outside, so the first and last letters
yielding means giving up, so the piece drops a letter

parts.note: tempo is the speed or time of a piece of music
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An addict's habit drags on, time and again, with nothing to show for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' suggests drugs alongside 'addict', but it means a try. The second 'time' is the musical tempo, which 'yielding' strips of its O.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a crack at something is to have a go, so crack is an informal word for a try or effort.

clue.text: Show bottom's not new low

indicators.note: not says the following piece must be absent from the word

parts.note: to moon is to bare one's backside

explanation.surface: Baring one's behind is old hat, not new, and rather base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective meaning base, but it is a verb noun, the call of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: To low is to make the deep sound cattle make, and the cow's call is spelt as this word.

clue.text: Nomadic Danes go here regularly

indicators.note: nomadic means wandering, so the picked letters wander into a new order
regularly takes every other letter, here the first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: Travelling Danes often head to this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes D, N, S, O, E, E from DANES GO HERE; 'Nomadic' rearranges them. The whole clue also points to a Danish city where Danes roam.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the third-largest city of Denmark, on the island of Funen, so it is a place Danes travel to.

clue.text: Refuse to be guilty of excessive consumption

definitions.meaning: a noun here: rubbish, things thrown away
to use something extravagantly or squander it

explanation.surface: Turning down food is wasteful overindulgence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for discarded rubbish and a verb for using resources carelessly or squandering them.

clue.text: He can't be trusted with artist's support

parts.note: an easel is the stand that holds a painter's canvas

explanation.surface: A painter's prop goes with an untrustworthy man.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is figuratively a sly, deceitful person, someone not to be relied on.

clue.text: Dance act raises sequence of steps to new level

definitions.text: sequence of steps to new level

indicators.note: to dance is to move about, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A dance routine takes its moves up a notch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance' rearranges ACT and RAISES together; 'steps' suggests dance steps but means stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is a run of treads leading to another floor of a building.

clue.text: Counsel against getting involved in a game of chance

indicators.note: getting involved in places a piece inside another

parts.note: dice is a gambling game played by throwing cubes
V is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A warning not to get drawn into gambling.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes inside A DICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel as a noun means guidance offered to someone, which is a synonym for recommendations.

clue.text: Person objecting to previous and current things for starters

parts.note: an anti is someone opposed to something
past means earlier, previous
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A dissenter objects to both old and modern ways at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' suggests 'to begin with' but means first courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: These Italian appetisers are served before the main meal, the dishes eaten as a first course.

clue.text: Distress is something quite clear to the audience

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is taken by its spoken form

parts.note: a pane of glass is transparent

explanation.surface: Suffering is plain for all to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress and suffering are near synonyms, covering both physical hurt and mental anguish.

clue.text: Forward's goal topped by striker's header

indicators.note: in a down answer, topped by puts the other piece above
a header is what heads something, so the first letter

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A football forward scores from a header by the striker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward', 'goal', 'striker' and 'header' all paint football, but 'Forward' is the verb meaning dispatch.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a letter is to dispatch it onward, which is what send means.

clue.text: Seasonal workers understand about very large wheels

indicators.note: wheels as a verb means turns round, so the whole is reversed
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in I see
VL is an abbreviation for very large

explanation.surface: Christmas temps spinning big wheels at a fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' looks like a noun but is the verb 'turns round', reversing everything to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are Santa's helpers who make toys at Christmas, so they are workers for the festive season.

clue.text: Writer about to back revolutionary book's sentiment

indicators.note: to back means to come behind, so these pieces follow
revolutionary means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book
the writer of a clue refers to themselves as I
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: An author returns to the feeling behind a radical book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns TOME into EMOT; I and ON go behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is a feeling or attitude, so it is a synonym for a strong feeling.

clue.text: Inexperienced person unable to get a grip?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., without the bench tool that clamps work

explanation.surface: A beginner who cannot get to grips with things.
explanation.walkthrough: A vice is a workshop clamp; having none, you cannot grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a beginner, someone new to an activity with little experience.
